answer: One defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent locks a deposit to its public key before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if the identity is proven duplicated. An honest agent pays one bond; an attacker minting a thousand fakes must lock a thousand bonds, so each fake becomes a costly signal instead of a free account. Auditors follow one suspicious thread -- shared funding, identical timing -- and forge the evidence into a slashing proof that burns the whole cluster's stake at once, turning Sybil farming from cheap spam into an expensive gamble.
